issues.legal_issue: The statutory consequences of repeal continue to apply when a repealed enactment is replaced by fresh legislation on the same subject unless the new legislation shows a contrary intention.
material_facts: A temporary ordinance made filing false information about a refugee land claim an offence.
The respondent filed a claim under the ordinance, and the claim was found to be false.
The ordinance was repealed and its provisions were re-enacted in a new Act.
The new Act treated earlier claims as claims under the Act and retained provisions for investigating claims, punishing false information, and cancelling allotments obtained on false claims.
The prosecution was begun after the repeal for the false claim filed while the ordinance was in force.
issues.conclusion: The repeal did not extinguish the liability incurred under the ordinance. The General Clauses Act applied despite the simultaneous re-enactment, because the new legislation did not manifest an intention to end that liability.
issues.legal_principle: General Clauses Act, 1897, section 6(c), (d) and (e), preserves accrued liabilities, penalties and proceedings on repeal unless a contrary intention appears; section 30 extends the Act to ordinances. The corresponding provision is section 4 of the Punjab General Clauses Act. When repeal is followed by fresh legislation on the same subject, the new legislation must be examined to determine whether it manifests an intention incompatible with the statutory savings; the question is not whether it expressly preserves old liabilities, and the absence of an express saving clause is not decisive. The Court rejected the broad dictum in Danmal Parshotamdas v. Baburam (1935) I.L.R. 58 All. 495 that section 6 does not apply to repeal followed by substitution.

rule.if: prosecution_for_pre_repeal_offense and enactment_repealed_and_replaced and successor_continues_claim_framework and successor_shows_no_incompatible_intention

predicates.prosecution_for_pre_repeal_offense: A prosecution was brought for conduct that occurred before the enactment under which the conduct was criminal was repealed.
predicates.enactment_repealed_and_replaced: The enactment was repealed and fresh legislation on the same subject took its place.
predicates.successor_continues_claim_framework: The replacement legislation continued to recognize claims made under the former enactment and retained mechanisms to investigate and address false claims.
predicates.successor_shows_no_incompatible_intentio: The replacement legislation did not show an intention to extinguish liabilities incurred under the former enactment.

issues.definition: When a prosecution concerns a pre-repeal offense and replacement legislation continues the relevant framework without showing an intention to end the old liability, that liability survives the repeal.

issues.legal_issue: The statutory consequences of repeal apply to a temporary enactment repealed before its scheduled expiry, but not to a temporary enactment that simply expires by efflux of time.
material_facts: The ordinance was temporary, but its prescribed period had not expired when it was repealed by the new Act.
The respondent's alleged offense occurred while the ordinance was in force.
The prosecution was initiated after the repeal.
issues.conclusion: Because the ordinance was repealed before it expired by efflux of time, the General Clauses Act applied and a prosecution for an offense committed under the ordinance could validly be started after repeal.
issues.legal_principle: General Clauses Act, 1897, section 6 applies when an enactment is repealed, including a temporary enactment repealed before its scheduled expiry. It does not apply when a temporary enactment automatically expires by efflux of time. Section 30 applies the General Clauses Act to ordinances.

rule.if: prosecution_for_offense_under_temporary_law and offense_preceded_repeal and temporary_law_repealed_before_expiry and prosecution_followed_repeal

predicates.prosecution_for_offense_under_temporary_: The proceeding is a prosecution for an offense created by a temporary enactment.
predicates.offense_preceded_repeal: The alleged offense occurred while the temporary enactment was in force and before its repeal.
predicates.temporary_law_repealed_before_expiry: The temporary enactment was formally repealed before the time for which it was to operate had run out.
predicates.prosecution_followed_repeal: The prosecution was initiated after the temporary enactment was repealed.

issues.definition: A prosecution initiated after repeal is valid when the offense was committed under a temporary enactment that was repealed before its scheduled expiry.

issues.legal_issue: A reference to things done under an enactment in a successor statute's saving language covers official acts done under the enactment, not a person's act in contravention of it.
material_facts: The respondent filed a false land claim under the ordinance.
The successor Act's saving language referred to rules, notifications, things done, and action taken in exercise of powers under the ordinance.
The Act separately provided that a refugee who had already submitted a claim under the ordinance was not to submit another claim for the same land.
issues.conclusion: The false claim was not an official act covered by the phrase 'anything done' in the saving language. However, under the Act's separate claim provision, an earlier claim under the ordinance was treated as a claim under the Act.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11 of the East Punjab Refugees (Registration of Land Claims) Act, 1948, saved rules, notifications and other official acts done in exercise of powers under the ordinance; 'anything done' did not include a person's act in contravention of the ordinance. The proviso to section 4 treated a previously submitted claim as a claim under the Act. Danmal Parshotamdas v. Baburam (1935) I.L.R. 58 All. 495 was discussed in connection with the broader repeal question, but did not govern this interpretation.

predicates.private_contravention_under_prior_enactm: A person performed an act in violation of the former enactment rather than an act in the exercise of powers under it.
predicates.saving_language_concerns_official_exerci: The successor legislation's saving language concerns acts performed in the exercise of official powers under the former enactment.

issues.definition: A person's act violating the former enactment is not treated as saved official action when the saving language concerns acts performed in the exercise of official powers.
